title: Fossils
description: Fossils are remains or imprints of organisms from long ago, preserved in rock. Scientists study fossils to learn about ancient life and how organisms have changed over time.

exercises.question: What is a FOSSIL?
choices: a living dinosaur
preserved remains or imprints of ancient organisms found in rock
a type of crystal
a very old tree
exercises.exp: Fossils are the preserved remains, imprints, or traces of organisms that lived millions of years ago.

exercises.question: How are FOSSILS usually formed?
choices: organisms are preserved in ice only
when dead organisms are quickly buried by sediment, hardening over millions of years
by animals digging and burying bones
scientists create them in labs
exercises.exp: When organisms die and are quickly buried by sediment (mud, sand), they can become fossilised over millions of years.

exercises.question: Scientists who study fossils are called ___.
choices: geologists
ecologists
palaeontologists
meteorologists
exercises.exp: Palaeontologists study fossils to learn about ancient life on Earth.

exercises.question: A fossil fish looks similar to fish today. What does this tell us?
choices: fish have not existed for long
fish have changed very little over millions of years
all fish are now extinct
fossils are not accurate
exercises.exp: When fossils closely match modern organisms, it suggests the species has changed little over time — it was well-adapted!

exercises.question: Scientists find a fossil tooth. It is sharp and pointed. What does this suggest?
choices: the animal ate only plants
the animal was a meat-eater (carnivore)
the animal never ate anything
it is a plant fossil
exercises.exp: Sharp, pointed teeth are adapted for tearing meat — the fossil likely belonged to a carnivore.

exercises.question: Fossils are most commonly found in ___.
choices: granite and marble rocks
sedimentary rocks like limestone and sandstone
ocean water
tree bark
exercises.exp: Sedimentary rocks form in layers from compressed sediment — fossils are trapped in these layers!

exercises.question: Rock layers (strata) tell us ___.
choices: how heavy rocks are
deeper layers are generally OLDER than upper layers
all rocks formed at the same time
which rocks are colourful
exercises.exp: The Law of Superposition: in undisturbed rock layers, older layers are at the bottom and newer layers are on top.

exercises.question: A fossil of a sea creature is found in the middle of a desert. What does this tell us?
choices: the animal swam through sand
that area was once covered by an ocean long ago
sea creatures live in deserts
the fossil was put there by humans
exercises.exp: Finding sea fossils inland tells us that the area was once an ancient ocean — Earth's surface has changed dramatically!

exercises.question: What can we LEARN from fossils?
choices: what ancient organisms looked like and how they lived
what ancient organisms thought about
what the weather was like every single day
what colours ancient organisms preferred
exercises.exp: Fossils give us evidence about body shape, size, diet, and habitat of ancient organisms.

exercises.question: How is a fossil DIFFERENT from a living organism?
choices: fossils are alive and growing
fossils are the preserved remains of organisms that lived long ago
fossils are found only in water
fossils are made of metal
exercises.exp: Fossils are not alive — they are the preserved remains or imprints of organisms from the past.

exercises.question: A rock layer with many fossils is found above a layer with NO fossils. What might this suggest?
choices: the top layer is older
something wiped out many organisms before the upper layer formed
fossils form on top of each other
all fossils form only in the top layer
exercises.exp: A gap in the fossil record could indicate a mass extinction or a period where organisms were not preserved.

exercises.question: Which is an example of a TRACE fossil?
choices: a preserved dinosaur bone
a dinosaur footprint in hardened rock
a fossil tooth
a preserved leaf shape
exercises.exp: Trace fossils are evidence of an organism's activity — footprints, burrows, and bite marks — not the body itself.

exercises.question: What is AMBER?
choices: a type of sedimentary rock
fossilised tree resin that can preserve insects and small organisms in incredible detail
a type of fossil tooth
a mineral found in caves only
exercises.exp: Amber is hardened ancient tree sap — insects, spiders, and plant material trapped in it can be preserved for millions of years in perfect detail!

exercises.question: Why are fossils of SOFT-BODIED animals (like worms and jellyfish) very RARE?
choices: soft animals never existed as fossils
soft bodies decay quickly and rarely leave remains — hard bones, shells, and teeth fossilise much more easily
all soft animals are still alive today
soft fossils dissolve in rainwater always
exercises.exp: Fossilisation is rare, and soft tissue almost never survives. Hard materials (bones, shells, teeth, wood) preserve much better. Soft-body fossils are extraordinary finds!

exercises.question: Scientists use CARBON DATING to determine the age of fossils. Carbon dating works by ___.
choices: counting growth rings in bones
measuring the decay of radioactive carbon-14 atoms in organic material
measuring the colour of the rock
weighing the fossil precisely
exercises.exp: Carbon-14 decays at a known rate. By measuring how much C-14 remains, scientists calculate how long ago the organism died — accurate up to ~50,000 years!

exercises.question: The CAMBRIAN EXPLOSION (about 540 million years ago) was ___.
choices: a massive volcanic eruption
a period when an enormous variety of animal body plans appeared in the fossil record in a geologically short time
a mass extinction event
the time when dinosaurs first appeared
exercises.exp: The Cambrian Explosion was a rapid burst of animal diversity — most major animal body plans appeared in the fossil record within a few million years. A pivotal event in life's history!

exercises.question: What does the fossil record tell us about the HISTORY OF LIFE?
choices: life on Earth has never changed
species have changed over time — some have gone extinct and new ones have appeared
all species alive today have always existed in the same form
fossils show life was always exactly like today
exercises.exp: The fossil record shows a clear history: simpler organisms first, then more complex ones, many extinct species, and gradual change over billions of years — evidence of evolution.

exercises.question: A fossil is found in a rock layer BELOW another fossil. The lower fossil is ___.
choices: newer than the upper fossil
the same age as the upper fossil
older than the upper fossil
impossible to date relative to the upper fossil
exercises.exp: Law of Superposition: lower = older. Sedimentary layers are deposited on top of each other over time — the bottom layers were laid first!

exercises.question: MASS EXTINCTIONS are shown in the fossil record as ___.
choices: gradual increases in species diversity
sudden disappearance of many species from fossil layers, followed by recovery of new species
fossils becoming more detailed
rock layers becoming thinner
exercises.exp: Mass extinction events appear in the fossil record as dramatic boundaries where many species suddenly disappear. There have been 5 major mass extinctions!

exercises.question: What can FOSSIL POLLEN tell scientists about ancient environments?
choices: what colour ancient flowers were
which types of plants lived in an area and what the climate was like thousands of years ago
how tall ancient trees were
the taste of ancient fruit
exercises.exp: Pollen preserves well and is species-specific. Ancient pollen cores from bogs and lake sediments reveal which plants grew in an area and track climate changes over thousands of years!

exercises.question: Why is the FOSSIL RECORD INCOMPLETE?
choices: scientists have not looked hard enough
fossilisation is rare — most organisms decompose completely. Only a tiny fraction are preserved under the right conditions
rocks are too hard to find fossils in
fossils are always destroyed by rain
exercises.exp: Fossilisation requires very specific conditions — quick burial, no scavengers, right chemistry. Most organisms leave no trace. What we find is just a tiny sample of ancient life!

exercises.question: Some fossils show organisms that lived only in COLD environments. These fossils are found in TROPICAL regions today. What does this tell us?
choices: cold-adapted animals lived in the tropics
Earth's climate was different in the past, OR the continents have moved since those organisms lived
tropical animals can survive cold climates
the fossils are fake
exercises.exp: Either ancient climates were different (ice ages extended further) or the continents have drifted (continental drift) — both explanations show Earth has changed dramatically.

exercises.question: A FOSSIL WHALE is found on top of a MOUNTAIN. What does this suggest?
choices: whales once lived on mountains
the mountain was once an ancient ocean floor — geological forces uplifted it over millions of years
the whale climbed the mountain
mountains form in oceans only
exercises.exp: Mountain-building processes can uplift ancient ocean floor sediments kilometres into the air. The Himalayas contain marine fossils — they were once an ancient seabed!

exercises.question: TRILOBITES were marine arthropods that lived 520-250 million years ago and then went EXTINCT. What can we conclude from their fossils?
choices: trilobites are still alive somewhere unknown
species can become extinct — the conditions that supported them no longer exist
fossils make living organisms extinct
trilobites are still evolving underground
exercises.exp: Trilobites dominated ancient seas for 270 million years then vanished in the Permian mass extinction. Their fossils are abundant — evidence of an important but extinct group.

exercises.question: Scientists can tell a lot from fossil TEETH. Flat grinding teeth suggest ___.
choices: the animal ate meat
the animal was a herbivore — flat teeth are for grinding plant material
the animal had no special diet
flat teeth mean the animal was aquatic
exercises.exp: Tooth shape = diet: flat molars for grinding plants (herbivores), sharp canines for tearing meat (carnivores), or mixed (omnivores). Fossil teeth are dietary clues!

exercises.question: COPROLITES are fossilised ___.
choices: eggs
footprints
droppings (faeces)
nests
exercises.exp: Coprolites are fossilised dung! They tell palaeontologists what ancient animals ate — undigested bone fragments, plant material, and shell pieces reveal diet directly.

exercises.question: A fossil is found with SIMILAR features to a modern organism but with notable differences. This is evidence of ___.
choices: the fossil is incorrectly identified
evolution — species change gradually over many generations
fossils are inaccurate representations
all species stay exactly the same forever
exercises.exp: Fossils showing gradual changes in body structure over time provide direct evidence that species evolve — accumulating small changes over many generations.

exercises.question: FEATHERED DINOSAUR fossils (like Archaeopteryx) were very important because they ___.
choices: proved dinosaurs could breathe underwater
showed a transitional form — features of both dinosaurs and birds, providing evidence that birds evolved from dinosaurs
proved feathers cannot fossilise
showed all birds are extinct
exercises.exp: Archaeopteryx had dinosaur features (teeth, clawed wings, long tail) AND bird features (feathers, wishbone). It is a classic transitional fossil linking dinosaurs to modern birds!

exercises.question: Why is RAPID BURIAL important for fossil formation?
choices: it crushes the organism into a flat shape for fossilisation
it protects the organism from scavengers and decomposers — increasing the chance of preservation
slow burial creates better fossils
rapid burial destroys all evidence of the organism
exercises.exp: If an organism is not quickly buried, scavengers eat it and bacteria decompose it. Quick burial by sediment preserves the body before it breaks down — key to fossilisation!

exercises.question: What is RELATIVE DATING of fossils?
choices: calculating the exact age in years using radioactive decay
estimating the age of fossils by comparing which rock layer they are found in (older layers = older fossils)
weighing the fossil to estimate age
measuring fossil size to determine age
exercises.exp: Relative dating uses rock layer position — lower = older, upper = younger. It tells us fossils are older OR younger than each other, not exact dates in years.

exercises.question: Some scientists study ANCIENT DNA extracted from fossils (like mammoths). What can this tell us?
choices: what the animal smelled like
genetic relationships to living animals, what the animal looked like, and evolutionary history
only the animal's diet
ancient DNA is too degraded to reveal anything useful
exercises.exp: Ancient DNA reveals genetic relationships — mammoths are closely related to Asian elephants. It can also reveal hair colour, size genes, and evolutionary branching points!

exercises.question: A FOSSIL is ___.
choices: any old rock
the preserved remains or traces of once-living organisms, usually found in sedimentary rock
an artificial copy of an ancient creature
a living organism that has not changed in millions of years
exercises.exp: Fossils preserve evidence of past life — bones, shells, imprints, footprints, even DNA in some cases. They are the pages of Earth's history book!

exercises.question: Fossils form most often in which type of rock?
choices: igneous (volcanic) rock
metamorphic (heat and pressure changed) rock
sedimentary rock — organisms are buried by sediment layers that slowly harden around them
all rock types equally
exercises.exp: Sedimentary rock forms in layers from settling particles. Organisms buried quickly by sediment are preserved as the sediment hardens into rock over millions of years.

exercises.question: TRACE FOSSILS include ___.
choices: only bones and teeth
only shells of sea creatures
footprints, burrows, eggs, coprolites (fossil dung) — evidence of behaviour, not just the organism itself
only imprints of leaves
exercises.exp: Trace fossils record behaviour — dinosaur footprints show how they walked, burrows reveal burrowing behaviour, coprolites reveal diet. Fascinating clues about ancient life!

exercises.question: RADIOCARBON DATING can estimate the age of organic material up to about ___.
choices: 1000 years
50,000 years — for older samples, other isotopes are used
1 million years
unlimited age
exercises.exp: Carbon-14 (radiocarbon) dating works up to ~50,000 years. Longer ages require potassium-argon or uranium-lead dating — which work for millions or billions of years!

exercises.question: HALF-LIFE is used in radiometric dating. It means ___.
choices: the age of the fossil divided by 2
the time required for half of a radioactive isotope to decay into a more stable form
half the amount of energy in the rock
the depth at which half the fossils are found
exercises.exp: Each radioactive isotope has a fixed half-life. By measuring how much of the original isotope remains, scientists calculate how many half-lives have passed — and therefore the age!

exercises.question: FOSSILS show that life on Earth has CHANGED OVER TIME. This is evidence for ___.
choices: life has always been the same
evolution — species change and new species arise as old ones go extinct over millions of years
fossils are always mistakes in the rock
life forms were created fully formed at a single point in time and never changed
exercises.exp: The fossil record shows a clear progression — simple single-celled organisms first, then increasingly complex life. Species appear and disappear over time — evolution!

exercises.question: The CAMBRIAN EXPLOSION (about 540 million years ago) was ___.
choices: a massive volcanic event that killed most life
a dramatic period when most animal body plans (phyla) first appeared in the fossil record over a few million years
the first appearance of plants on land
the extinction of the dinosaurs
exercises.exp: The Cambrian Explosion: complex multicellular animal life diversified explosively. Most modern animal body plans (arthropods, molluscs, chordates) appear in Cambrian fossils!

exercises.question: DINOSAURS are classified as ___.
choices: mammals
fish
extinct reptiles — closely related to modern birds, which evolved from theropod dinosaurs
amphibians that grew very large
exercises.exp: Dinosaurs were reptiles. Modern birds evolved from theropod dinosaurs — so technically, birds ARE living dinosaurs! Crocodiles are also close reptile relatives.

exercises.question: The MASS EXTINCTION 66 million years ago that killed non-avian dinosaurs was likely caused by ___.
choices: a massive ice age only
giant volcanic eruptions only
a large asteroid impact combined with volcanic activity — causing global cooling and ecosystem collapse
a pandemic disease that spread worldwide
exercises.exp: The Chicxulub asteroid impact (Mexico) caused fires, dust clouds blocking sunlight, and rapid cooling. This, combined with Deccan Traps volcanic activity, caused the K-Pg mass extinction!

exercises.question: LIVING FOSSILS are organisms that ___.
choices: have been brought back from extinction
look almost identical to their fossil ancestors from millions of years ago — barely changed by evolution
are partly alive and partly fossilised
are too recent to have fossils yet
exercises.exp: Living fossils: coelacanth fish (thought extinct 66 mya, rediscovered 1938), horseshoe crabs (450 million years old unchanged), and ginkgo trees all barely changed from their ancient ancestors!

exercises.question: AMBER is fossilised tree resin. What can perfectly preserved amber fossils reveal?
choices: only the colour of ancient trees
insects, spiders, feathers, pollen, and even DNA from organisms trapped millions of years ago
only large dinosaur bones
only the shapes of ancient tree bark
exercises.exp: Amber preserves organisms in extraordinary detail — soft tissues, behaviours, colours! A piece of 100-million-year-old amber held a baby bird and spider webs in incredible detail!

exercises.question: STRATIGRAPHY is the study of rock layers (strata). The principle of SUPERPOSITION states ___.
choices: fossils at the bottom are always younger
deeper layers are generally OLDER — they were deposited first and buried by later layers
all rock layers are the same age
deeper layers contain more fossils
exercises.exp: Superposition: deeper = older (unless layers have been overturned by tectonics). Comparing fossils in different layers reveals the order of life forms through time!

exercises.question: INDEX FOSSILS are ___.
choices: fossils that are always found at the same depth
fossils of organisms that lived in one small area only
fossils of organisms that existed for a SHORT time but were WIDESPREAD — used to precisely date rock layers
the largest fossils found in any rock layer
exercises.exp: Index fossils: widespread species that lived for a short geological time. Finding them in a rock layer pins down its age precisely — even across continents!

exercises.question: What is CONVERGENT EVOLUTION, shown in the fossil record?
choices: two species evolving to become different from each other
unrelated species evolving similar features independently because they face similar environments/challenges
identical fossils found on different continents
species that evolved from the same ancestor
exercises.exp: Convergent evolution: dolphins (mammals) and ichthyosaurs (ancient reptiles) evolved similar streamlined bodies independently — same aquatic challenge, same solution!

exercises.question: Why are SOFT-BODIED organisms rare in the fossil record?
choices: soft organisms never existed
soft tissue decays quickly — without hard parts (shells, bones) organisms rarely leave fossils
soft organisms live where no sediment is deposited
scientists have not looked in the right places yet
exercises.exp: Hard parts (bones, shells) resist decay and preserve well. Soft tissue decomposes rapidly. Exceptional preservation (Burgess Shale fossils) occasionally captures soft-bodied creatures!

exercises.question: The PERMIAN EXTINCTION (252 million years ago) was the WORST mass extinction — it killed about ___.
choices: 10% of all species
50% of all species
96% of marine species and 70% of land species
5% of species on Earth
exercises.exp: The Great Dying: Permian extinction wiped out ~96% of marine species. Likely caused by massive Siberian volcanic eruptions releasing CO₂ and SO₂, causing rapid climate change.

exercises.question: What do the FOSSIL RECORD and DNA evidence together confirm about evolution?
choices: species were created suddenly and never changed
all life on Earth is unrelated
species share common ancestors and have changed over billions of years — both types of evidence are consistent
only animals evolved, not plants
exercises.exp: Fossils show the progression of life forms over time. DNA analysis shows the genetic relationships between species. Both independently confirm common descent and evolutionary change!

exercises.question: BIOSTRATIGRAPHY uses fossils to ___.
choices: estimate the mass of prehistoric creatures
determine the age and correlation of rock strata around the world using characteristic fossil assemblages
identify which rocks contain oil
predict future evolutionary changes
exercises.exp: Biostratigraphy correlates rocks worldwide using fossils — if the same index fossil species appears in rocks in North America and Europe, those layers formed at the same time!

exercises.question: Which best explains why there are GAPS in the fossil record?
choices: palaeontologists have not found all fossils yet
most organisms die in conditions where fossilisation does not occur — fossilisation requires rapid burial in sediment, precise conditions, and millions of years
all organisms eventually fossilise
gaps prove evolution did not occur
exercises.exp: Fossilisation is rare — organisms must be buried quickly before decay, in sediment-depositing environments. Erosion also destroys fossils. The fossil record is amazing despite its incompleteness!
